ai.description: This small frog reaches 18–22 mm. It is yellowish-brown with a dark hourglass pattern on the back and a white belly. It features a pointed snout and lacks webbing on the fingers.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes parvulus* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow-orange coloration on the hidden surfaces of the thighs and groin, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes parvulus* inhabits evergreen forests and tea plantations in the Western Ghats, typically found on low-lying vegetation at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes parvulus is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small insects among the foliage of shrubs and low-hanging tree branches.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes parvulus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes parvulus* is found in the Western Ghats of India, specifically within the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Karin Bubble-nest Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like "tseep" sound, often repeated in short, rapid bursts while perched in shrubs or trees near forest streams.
